reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, a small campus by AI standards and one of only 19 Texas data centers that disclose power at all.

The pattern here is disclosure scarcity rather than capacity. Texas has 133 mapped facilities, but just 19 publish power figures, so any statewide total rests on a small minority of sites. SAT1's 9 MW ranks 14th among those disclosed sites and equals 1.9% of the 475 MW of IT load Texas operators have made public. Texas sits behind only California and Virginia in disclosed AI-relevant capacity, which says more about who reports than about who can supply power.

For AI specifically, 9 MW is a modest draw. A single large training cluster can exceed that on its own, so SAT1 is better suited to inference, smaller teams, or one node of a multi-site deployment. Its certifications, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FISMA, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II, TIA-942, point to regulated financial and government workloads rather than frontier model training. The 110,000 square feet of technical space against 9 MW works out to roughly 82 watts per square foot, and the estimate of about 225 racks assumes 40 kW per rack, an assumption about utilization rather than an operator figure.

What the data does not cover is the part that decides whether the power is actually usable. Backup generation, renewable sourcing, and grid interconnection are not disclosed, and neither is an announced expansion, which the suitability score of 56 lists as its missing input. Without those, a reader can compare SAT1 to other disclosed Texas sites but cannot judge its resilience, its energy source, or how long it would take to energize more load.
